newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Russia was helpful in Iraqi crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Russia was helpful in Iraqi crisis.

text.p: Despite harsh Russian criticism of the U.S. missile strike on Iraq, the United States said on Tuesday Moscow had played a useful role in the crisis and could continue to be helpful.
Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said the strikes "cannot be supported by anyone at all" and suggested they had been launched to help President Bill Clinton win re-election in November.

But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Washington had been in close contact with the Russians before the attack and Secretary of State Warren Christopher had exchanged letters with Primakov.

"On several occasions over the last two days, we did share with the Russians our appreciation of the need for action in this situation, and the Russians were not surprised by our action," Burns told a news briefing.

"I think we've had very good, constructive conversations with them, and the Russians were helpful over the weekend in relaying certain messages to the government of (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein," he said.

But the U.S. government was not surprised by the Russian statement and "had heard pretty much in private what you saw in public," Burns said. "What we hope now ... is that the Russian government will use whatever influence it has in Baghdad with the Saddam Hussein regime to counsel Saddam to withdraw completely from northern Iraq."

The United States launched the cruise missile strike on Tuesday, three days after Baghdad had moved troops into the Western-protected Kurdish region in northern Iraq, intervening in clashes between two warring Kurdish factions.
